references.text: The preceding verse tells us that the disciples were startled and afraid when Jesus appeared to them, which is the background for Jesus' question in verse 38 about why they are troubled ([ref:Luk 24:37|Luke 24:37]).
Mary was troubled (διεταράχθη) by the angel's greeting, a parallel to the disciples' disturbance (τεταραγμένοι) when encountering the divine ([ref:Luk 1:29|Luke 1:29]).
Jesus says "Let not your heart be troubled" (μὴ ταρασσέσθω ὑμῶν ἡ καρδία), using the same verb (ταράσσω) and theme of inner disturbance ([ref:Joh 14:1|John 14:1]).
Again, Jesus urges the disciples not to let their hearts be troubled or afraid (μὴ ταρασσέσθω ὑμῶν ἡ καρδία μηδὲ δειλιάτω), using the same verb ταράσσω ([ref:Joh 14:27|John 14:27]).

Jesus asks the scribes "Why do you reason these things in your hearts?" (τί ταῦτα διαλογίζεσθε ἐν ταῖς καρδίαις ὑμῶν), a close parallel to the expression about thoughts (διαλογισμοί) rising in the heart ([ref:Mark 2:6-8|Mark 2:6-8]).
Jesus recognizes the scribes' thoughts (διαλογισμούς) and asks "What are you reasoning in your hearts?", a thematic parallel with thoughts in the heart ([ref:Luk 5:22|Luke 5:22]).
Jesus knew their thoughts (διαλογισμοί), showing Jesus' ability to know what moves in people's hearts ([ref:Luk 6:8|Luke 6:8]).

God sees that the thoughts of a person's heart (מַחְשְׁבֹת לִבּוֹ) were continually only evil – a fundamental Old Testament parallel to the motif of thoughts or plans rising in the heart ([ref:1 Mos 6:5|Genesis 6:5]).

Daniel describes the thoughts that rose up in King Nebuchadnezzar's heart (מַחְשְׁבָתָךְ עַל־מִשְׁכְּבָךְ סְלִקוּ), a parallel to the expression about thoughts rising in the heart ([ref:Dan 2:29-30|Daniel 2:29-30]).

The disciples were startled when they saw Jesus walking on the water, and Jesus said "Take courage! It is I; do not be afraid!" – a similar situation where the disciples are troubled by Jesus' supernatural appearance ([ref:Mark 6:49-50|Mark 6:49-50]).

The disciples were disturbed (ἐταράχθησαν) when they saw Jesus walking on the sea, and Jesus comforted them – a close parallel where the same verb is used for the disciples' reaction ([ref:Matt 14:26-27|Matthew 14:26-27]).
